1.why: All screenshots show a static, uncluttered layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary buttons are solid blue, the active wizard step is filled dark blue, and success feedback is rendered in green so key elements stand out.

3.why: Numbered step indicator, clear page headings, single main form per screen, and persistent help panel let the user locate the needed action quickly.

4.why: A visible 5-step progress bar and a ‘Next:’ banner on every screen remove the need to remember the overall sequence or rules.

5.why: No ‘remember me’ checkbox, password-manager affordance, or autofill prompt appears on any sign-in or password field.

6.why: The UI never surfaces previously saved accounts, familiar devices, or other recognizable saved items.

7.why: Copy throughout uses short, plain sentences such as ‘Take one step at a time’ and ‘Recovery complete. Your next step is to sign in.’

8.why: No error or validation-failure messages appear in any of the fourteen screenshots, so their clarity cannot be verified.

9.why: Password composition rules are stated and Logs display the exact practice codes to type, although no sample email or password strings are given.

10.why: Only password-plus-security-code is offered; no alternative methods (face, passkey, etc.) or choice among them are presented.

11.why: Each screen contains a single primary task with at most two input fields and one main call-to-action button.

12.why: Green confirmation text after every action (e.g., ‘Password confirmed’, ‘Privacy conditions accepted’) explicitly states the outcome.

13.why: Every page includes both a ‘Next:’ tip banner and an expanded ‘Help and safe sign-in reminders’ section.

14.why: Input fields stay editable, resend/confirm buttons remain active, and no lock-out or timeout is shown, allowing re-attempts without friction.

15.why: Header, navigation links, help panel, button style, card layout and Logs section are identical across all steps.
